body:
Bundle of standard-practice hardening gaps found in security review (none are
spec violations; spec §10 delegates transport/rate-limiting to the proxy, but
these belong in the app layer):

1. change-password (accounts.py) leaves every other session's token valid. If
   you're changing a password because a device/token may be compromised, that
   defeats the purpose. Standard: revoke all auth_tokens for the account
   except the one making the change (session list UI already distinguishes
   'current'). Consider same-but-optional on change-email.
2. No MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH anywhere: unbounded request bodies hit
   request.get_json() — /sync will happily buffer arbitrarily large payloads.
   Set a sane app-level default in create_blueprint's record_once (e.g. a few
   MB, sized to realistic sync batches) so self-hosters get protection even
   without proxy tuning; document override.
3. HTML-serving routes (invite landing page, embedded web app index) send no
   security headers. Add at least Content-Security-Policy (SPA is fully
   self-contained: default-src 'self' plus what Vite's output needs),
   X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, and
   Referrer-Policy — the invite URL path contains the secret token, so
   Referrer-Policy: no-referrer on the landing page matters most.
4. Document (README "Deployment requirements"): register/login responses
   permit account enumeration (409 email_taken; accepted trade-off, no email
   infra for the alternative) — state it explicitly so operators know.
Files: accounts.py (+tests for 1), __init__.py (2,3), templates/invite.html
headers via after_request or explicit response headers, README.md (4).
title: Server hardening: revoke sessions on password change, request size cap, security headers
